title: Observation of CH<SUB>3</SUB><SUP>17</SUP>OH and CH<SUB>3</SUB><SUP>18</SUP>OH in Orion KL: A new tool to study star formation history
question: Is CH3(17)OH present in the ISM (Orion KL), and what are the CH3(18)OH/CH3(17)OH, 16O/17O and 16O/18O isotope ratios in methanol

data.angular_resolution: 2013.1.00553.S cube: 1.7" x 1.0" PA = 87.6 deg; SV cube: 1.9" x 1.4" PA = -12.8 deg; convolved to 2.0" x 2.0" for line comparison

evidence.quote: we utilized the line parameters of CH$_3$$^{17}$OH by (cite: Tamanai2025) and those in CDMS for CH$_3$$^{18}$OH

what.value: CH3OH column densities and rotational temperatures at dM-1 and dM-3 (rotation temperatures 130 K and 58 K)

evidence.quote: using the column densities and rotational temperatures of CH$_3$OH at dM-1 and dM-3 from (cite: Peng2012)
In the calculation, we assumed the rotation temperature of 58 K and 130 K for MeOH1 and MeOH2, respectively, which are the rotation temperatures of CH$_3$OH in dM-3 and dM-1 (cite: Peng2012).

what.value: Canonical 16O/18O = 560 and 16O/17O = 2000 (local ISM), used for the optical-depth estimate and comparison

evidence.quote: Assuming the canonical values of $^{16}$O/$^{18}$O $=560$ and $^{16}$O/$^{17}$O $=2000$ (cite: Wilson1999)

what.value: H2 volume density > 1e8 cm^-3 used to justify LTE

evidence.quote: the assumption of LTE is justified because the emissions originate from sufficiently dense regions with the H$_2$ volume density of $n_{\rm H_2} > 10^8$ cm$^{-3}$ (cite: Favre2011)

what.value: Einstein A and C coefficients for the critical-density estimate of CH3OH (5_0-4_0, E) at 100 K

evidence.quote: from Leiden Atomic and Molecular Database (cite: Schoier2005)

what.value: 18O/17O = 3.6 +/- 0.7 from C18O and C17O J=5-4 with Odin toward Orion KL (comparison)

evidence.quote: (cite: Persson2007) evaluated the $^{18}$O/$^{17}$O ratio of $3.6 \pm 0.7$ by using C$^{18}$O($J=5-4$)

what.value: 18O/17O = 4.1 (+2.1/-1.3) in the Compact Ridge from Herschel/HIFI CO isotopologues (comparison)

evidence.quote: (cite: Plume2012) derived the $^{18}$O/$^{17}$O ratio of $4.1^{+2.1}_{-1.3}$ in the Compact Ridge
(cite: Zou2023) estimated the $^{18}$O/$^{17}$O ratio of $4.1\pm0.1$ in G209.00-19.38 in Orion Nebula

what.value: 16O/18O ~ 218 from methyl formate isotopologues toward Orion KL (comparison)

evidence.quote: which estimated the $^{16}$O/$^{18}$O ratio to be $\sim 218$ from the total column density of the two isotopomer HC$^{18}$OOCH$_3$ and HCO$^{18}$OCH$_3$

recipe.goal: Calibrate and image the archival cubes and continuum
recipe.method: Calibrated visibilities (observatory script / SV data), continuum subtracted with a 0th-order polynomial fit to line-free channels, CLEAN with Briggs robust 0.5, primary-beam correction with impbcor
key_parameters: Briggs robust = 0.5; 488 kHz frequency resolution; cube rms 7 mJy/beam (2013.1.00553.S) and 12 mJy/beam (SV)

recipe.method: Integrated intensity map of CH3(18)OH 5_0-4_0 E over 4.5-11.5 km/s; two peaks MeOH1 and MeOH2 coincident with methyl formate peaks MF1 and MF2
Compare observed spectra at MeOH1 and MeOH2 to the laboratory CH3(17)OH spectrum and frequencies; assign other lines with CDMS and JPL catalogues; compare profiles and maps with CH3(18)OH
key_parameters: Six CH3(17)OH lines identified at S/N more than 50 sigma; 5_2-4_2 A- blended with 5_3-4_3 E at 236.554 GHz

recipe.goal: Match angular resolution for line comparison
recipe.method: Convolve cubes with Gaussian kernels to a common 2.0" x 2.0" resolution

recipe.goal: Derive CH3(18)OH and CH3(17)OH column densities and their ratio at MeOH1 and MeOH2
recipe.method: LTE, optically thin, single-transition (5_0-4_0 E) integrated intensities from the 2.0" x 2.0" cubes with fixed rotation temperatures
key_parameters: Rotation temperature 58 K (MeOH1) and 130 K (MeOH2), fixed
assumptions: LTE justified by dense gas (n_H2 > 1e8 cm^-3 vs n_crit ~1e5 cm^-3); optically thin lines

recipe.method: Estimate optical depths of CH3(18)OH and CH3(17)OH 5_0-4_0 E from Peng2012 CH3OH column densities and rotational temperatures with canonical 16O/18O = 560 and 16O/17O = 2000
assumptions: Isotopologue ratios equal the canonical local-ISM values

recipe.goal: Derive 16O/17O and 16O/18O at dM-1 and dM-3 using Peng2012 CH3OH
recipe.method: Smooth the ALMA data to 3.8" x 2.0" PA 22 deg, repeat the LTE column-density procedure with Trot 130 K (dM-1) and 58 K (dM-3), and combine with CH3OH column densities to form isotope ratios
assumptions: CH3OH column densities from Peng2012 (optical depth below 0.2) are applicable at the ALMA positions, which coincide with the PdBI positions within the beam

answer_key.quantity: CH3(18)OH/CH3(17)OH ratio at MeOH1 and MeOH2 (2.0" x 2.0")
